title: WebAssembly
text: A portable binary instruction format that runs code from many languages at near-native speed inside a sandbox.

title: WASI
text: The WebAssembly System Interface gives sandboxed programs controlled access to files, clocks, random numbers and other operating system features.

title: WASIX
text: An extension of WASI that adds threads, sockets, process forking and other POSIX features so existing server software can run as WebAssembly.

title: Edge computing
text: Running code in data centers close to users instead of one central region, which cuts network latency.

title: Cold start
text: The delay before the first request is answered while a new instance loads code, starts the runtime and warms caches.

title: Scale to zero
text: Stopping every instance of an idle app so it uses no compute, then starting one again when the next request arrives.

title: Autoscaling
text: Adding or removing instances automatically as traffic rises and falls.

title: Load balancer
text: A component that spreads incoming requests across several servers so no single one is overloaded.

title: CDN
text: A content delivery network caches static files on servers around the world so pages load quickly everywhere.

title: DNS
text: The Domain Name System translates human-readable names such as example.com into IP addresses.

title: TLS certificate
text: A signed file that proves a server owns a domain and lets browsers open an encrypted HTTPS connection.

title: HTTP status code
text: A three-digit number in every response: 2xx means success, 4xx a client error and 5xx a server error.

title: REST API
text: An interface where clients read and change resources with standard HTTP methods such as GET, POST, PUT and DELETE.

title: GraphQL
text: A query language that lets clients ask an API for exactly the fields they need in a single request.

title: WebSocket
text: A protocol that keeps one connection open so the server and browser can send messages to each other at any time.

title: Rate limiting
text: Capping how many requests a client may make in a time window to protect a service from abuse or overload.

title: Caching
text: Storing the result of expensive work so repeated requests can be answered faster.

title: Environment variable
text: A named value supplied to a process at start, often used for configuration and secrets instead of hard-coding them.

title: Secret
text: A sensitive value such as an API key or database password that must be stored encrypted and never committed to source control.

title: Container
text: A packaged application with its dependencies that runs isolated from other processes on a shared operating system kernel.

title: Virtual machine
text: An emulated computer with its own operating system kernel, giving strong isolation at the cost of slower boot and more memory.

title: Sandbox
text: A restricted environment where code can only reach the resources it has been explicitly granted.

title: Runtime
text: The software that loads and executes a program, such as a JavaScript engine, the Python interpreter or a WebAssembly runtime.

title: Package registry
text: A service that hosts versioned packages so tools can download dependencies by name.

title: Lockfile
text: A file that records the exact dependency versions installed, so every build gets the same packages.

title: Semantic versioning
text: A version scheme of MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH where breaking changes bump the major number.

title: Continuous integration
text: Automatically building and testing every change pushed to a repository.

title: Continuous deployment
text: Automatically releasing every change that passes the pipeline to production.

title: Blue-green deployment
text: Running the new version beside the old one and switching traffic over at once, which allows instant rollback.

title: Rollback
text: Returning an application to a previous known-good release after a bad deploy.

title: Health check
text: A periodic request that tells the platform whether an instance is alive and ready to receive traffic.

title: Logs
text: Timestamped text records a program writes while running, used to debug errors after the fact.

title: Metrics
text: Numeric measurements over time, such as request count, latency and memory use, shown on dashboards and alerts.

title: Tracing
text: Following one request through every service it touches to find where time is spent.

title: Latency
text: The time between sending a request and receiving its response, usually measured in milliseconds.

title: Throughput
text: How much work a system completes per unit of time, for example requests per second.

title: Concurrency
text: Making progress on several tasks during overlapping periods, for example by switching between them while each waits on I/O.

title: Parallelism
text: Running several computations at exactly the same time on multiple CPU cores.

title: Stateless service
text: A service that keeps no data between requests, so any instance can answer any request and scaling is easy.

title: Persistent volume
text: Disk storage that survives restarts so an application can keep files between runs.

title: Object storage
text: Storage for files addressed by key in buckets, built to hold huge amounts of unstructured data cheaply.

title: Relational database
text: A database that stores data in tables with rows and columns and is queried with SQL.

title: SQL
text: Structured Query Language, used to read and change data in relational databases.

title: Index
text: A data structure that lets a database find rows without scanning the whole table.

title: Database migration
text: A versioned script that changes a database schema, such as adding a table or a column.

title: Connection pool
text: A set of reusable database connections shared by requests, avoiding the cost of opening a new one each time.

title: Transaction
text: A group of database operations that either all succeed or all fail together.

title: Key-value store
text: A database that stores values under unique keys and is optimized for very fast reads and writes.

title: Message queue
text: A buffer that lets one service hand off work to another asynchronously, so slow tasks do not block requests.

title: Cron job
text: A task scheduled to run automatically at fixed times or intervals.

title: Webhook
text: An HTTP request one service sends to another to report that an event happened.

title: OAuth
text: An authorization standard that lets users grant an app limited access to their account on another service without sharing a password.

title: Authentication
text: Verifying who a user or service is, for example with a password, passkey or token.

title: Authorization
text: Deciding what an authenticated user or service is allowed to do.

title: JSON Web Token
text: A compact, signed token carrying claims about a user, often sent in the Authorization header.

title: CORS
text: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing is a browser rule that controls which other websites may call an API from JavaScript.

title: Custom domain
text: Serving an app from a domain you own instead of the platform's default address.

title: Reverse proxy
text: A server that receives client requests and forwards them to one or more backend servers.

title: Static site
text: A website made only of prebuilt HTML, CSS, JavaScript and images, served without running server code.

title: Server-side rendering
text: Generating a page's HTML on the server for each request so content appears before JavaScript loads.

title: Single-page application
text: A web app that loads one HTML page and updates it with JavaScript as the user navigates.

title: Serverless function
text: A small piece of code the platform runs on demand per request, without the developer managing servers.

title: Infrastructure as code
text: Describing servers, networks and services in versioned configuration files instead of setting them up by hand.

title: Monorepo
text: One repository that holds many projects, sharing tooling and making cross-project changes atomic.

title: Embedding
text: A list of numbers that represents the meaning of a text, so similar texts end up close together.

title: Semantic search
text: Finding documents by meaning rather than exact keywords, by comparing the embedding of a query with document embeddings.

title: Cosine similarity
text: A score between -1 and 1 that measures how closely two vectors point in the same direction.

title: Vector database
text: A database that stores embeddings and quickly finds the ones nearest to a query vector.

title: Keyword search
text: Finding documents that contain the exact words of a query, often ranked with formulas such as BM25.

title: Retrieval-augmented generation
text: Giving a language model relevant documents found by search so its answer is grounded in your own data.

title: Large language model
text: A neural network trained on large amounts of text that can generate and transform language.

title: Tokenizer
text: A component that splits text into tokens, the small units a language model reads.

title: Inference
text: Running a trained model on new input to produce a prediction, as opposed to training it.

title: ONNX
text: Open Neural Network Exchange, a file format for machine learning models that many runtimes can execute.

title: Quantization
text: Storing model weights with fewer bits, such as 8-bit integers, to make the model smaller and faster with a small loss in accuracy.

title: Fine-tuning
text: Continuing to train a pretrained model on a smaller dataset so it performs better on a specific task.

title: GPU
text: A graphics processing unit with thousands of cores, widely used to train and run neural networks.

title: Memory limit
text: The maximum RAM an instance may use before the platform stops it.

title: Out of memory
text: An error raised when a program requests more memory than is available, often ending the process.

title: Timeout
text: The longest time a request is allowed to run before it is cancelled.

title: Idempotency
text: The property that repeating an operation has the same effect as doing it once, which makes retries safe.

title: Retry with backoff
text: Repeating a failed request after waiting progressively longer each time.

title: Feature flag
text: A switch that turns functionality on or off at runtime without deploying new code.

title: Uptime
text: The share of time a service is available, often promised in a service level agreement such as 99.9 percent.

title: Multi-region
text: Running an application in several geographic regions for lower latency and resilience to regional outages.

title: Bandwidth
text: The amount of data transferred to and from an application, often billed per gigabyte.
